output.metric: Daily totals exceed the weekly rollup
output.observed_change: For the week of 2026-06-22, summing the daily signup table gives about a third more signups than the weekly rollup reports for the same week.
output.notes: A genuine marketing campaign started mid-window.

blind_spots: marts.signups has no owners registered in DataHub — the ownership lookup returned the entity with no owners field. Accountability gap; recorded as a finding, not a clean result.
marts.signups schema has zero fields recorded in DataHub (datahub.schema returned totalFields=0). No column-level metadata for the metric itself; the view text is the only source of its shape.

DataHub lineage lists raw.web_sessions as an upstream of staging.events_daily, but the events_daily view SQL only references channel_events_raw. The web_sessions edge is unconfirmed / possibly stale — it may not actually feed the daily signup count, despite its 'is_automated flag that not every producer sets' description inviting a bot-filtering story.

The weekly rollup used in the comparison (events_weekly_rollup) is NOT catalogued in DataHub — searches for 'weekly signup rollup' and 'signup' returned no rollup entity. No lineage/ownership/schema metadata exists for the weekly comparison series; only the warehouse view text is available. Note the daily and weekly views both derive from channel_events_raw but bucket differently (events_daily: date(occurred_at,'+9 hours'); events_weekly_rollup: strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) with no offset).
Raw postgres source tables (channel_events_raw, web_sessions) have no column schema pulled — only descriptions. occurred_at column type and timezone semantics at the source are unverified.

Schema- and definition-change history not pulled (schema_migration_log, metric_definition_history, release_deploy_log tables not queried). Cannot yet state whether a bucketing or definition change landed inside the day 1–36 window, which overlaps the mid-window marketing campaign named in the symptom.

output.statement: The daily signup table and events_weekly_rollup apply incompatible time-bucketing definitions over the same channel_events_raw source — events_daily buckets by KST calendar date via date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') while events_weekly_rollup buckets by UTC week via strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) with no offset — so the seven daily rows summed for the week of 2026-06-22 cover a different set of raw event rows than the weekly bucket, and the ~1/3 excess is this boundary/definition artifact (amplified by the mid-window campaign surge landing on the ~9h-to-1-day misaligned week edge), not a real signup difference.
would_be_confirmed_by: Mapping each raw channel_events_raw row to both its events_daily week-window and its events_weekly_rollup week bucket shows a block of rows assigned to the week-of-2026-06-22 daily window but to an adjacent bucket by the weekly rollup, and that block's count ≈ the observed excess (~1/3)
Re-running the weekly rollup with the +9h offset (matching events_daily) closes the daily-sum-vs-weekly gap to near zero
The excess rows cluster near the week boundary (first/last KST day of the week) rather than interior days
would_be_refuted_by: Re-bucketing channel_events_raw with a single identical time definition (same offset AND same week anchor) for both series still leaves a ~1/3 gap for the week of 2026-06-22
Inspection of the two view definitions shows they actually apply the same time-bucketing (e.g. both +9h or both no offset), so the quoted SQL divergence is not real

Assigning each raw event to a week under both definitions shows the daily and weekly windows cover the identical set of raw rows (no rows shift across the boundary), leaving no set difference to explain the excess
The excess signups fall on interior days far from any week boundary, where a ≤1-day offset misalignment cannot reassign them between buckets

output.statement: marts.signups over-counts because the daily-only transformation (channel_events_raw -> staging.events_daily) multiplies rows per underlying signup — most plausibly via the raw.web_sessions upstream that DataHub lineage records but the current events_daily view text omits (a one-event-to-many-sessions fan-out join), or via un-deduplicated at-least-once event ingestion — so summing the seven daily rows for the week of 2026-06-22 counts events that events_weekly_rollup (reading channel_events_raw directly, without that fan-out) counts once, producing the ~1/3 excess as a duplication/fan-out data defect rather than a bucketing or behavioural effect.
would_be_confirmed_by: In staging.events_daily (or its compiled SQL), the event count for the week exceeds channel_events_raw's count of distinct event_ids for the same rows, i.e. COUNT(*) > COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) on the daily path.
The running events_daily model actually references/joins raw.web_sessions, and web_sessions holds multiple rows per event key, producing the fan-out.
daily_sum / count(distinct event_id) for the week is approximately 1.33, matching the observed excess.
channel_events_raw contains duplicate event_id rows for the week that events_weekly_rollup collapses but staging.events_daily retains.
would_be_refuted_by: COUNT(*) equals COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) in both channel_events_raw and staging.events_daily for the week of 2026-06-22 — no duplication or fan-out is present.
staging.events_daily's total event count for the week equals channel_events_raw's event count for the same rows (strict 1:1, no row multiplication).
The compiled/executed events_daily model references only channel_events_raw with no join to web_sessions or any other table and no UNION/self-join, so no row-duplicating mechanism exists.
The full daily-vs-weekly gap is explained by identical distinct-event counts on both sides landing in different week buckets (boundary reassignment) — the excess is bucketing, not duplication.
The excess is not a stable ~1.33 per-row multiplier but varies arbitrarily across rows/days in a way inconsistent with row duplication.

output.statement: The ~1/3 daily-over-weekly excess for the week of 2026-06-22 is a measurement artifact of the events_weekly_rollup instrument itself — not of the source data or the bucketing logic — because that rollup is an uncatalogued materialized snapshot (no DataHub lineage, owner, or refresh SLA) whose stored value for that week was frozen from an incomplete or partially-failed load (a late/dropped partition or a job that errored or timed out mid-run during the campaign traffic spike and was never re-materialized), so it under-reports the true count that the daily table, rebuilt each day, correctly carries.
would_be_confirmed_by: The rollup's last-build timestamp or partition watermark for the week of 2026-06-22 predates the arrival of part of that week's channel_events_raw events, and simply re-running the rollup raises its count to match the summed daily rows.

Only the campaign-affected week(s) diverge while every other week reconciles between daily and weekly, isolating the fault to a specific failed or incomplete materialization event rather than a systematic rule difference.
Job/orchestration logs show an error, timeout, retry, or skipped partition for the events_weekly_rollup build during the campaign spike.
would_be_refuted_by: Re-materializing events_weekly_rollup from its current source input reproduces the same ~1/3 shortfall versus the summed daily rows — the gap is stable under recomputation, so nothing was frozen from an incomplete load.

Recomputing the weekly figure with the daily table's own KST date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') bucketing closes the gap, showing the discrepancy is definitional (bucketing mismatch), not an instrument fault.
Non-campaign weeks outside the surge show the same daily-over-weekly ratio, indicating a persistent structural gap rather than a one-week load failure.

The rollup's build/job history shows a clean, complete run for the week of 2026-06-22 with no failed/partial materialization, dropped partition, or late-arriving data, and its stored count matches an independent fresh COUNT over the same UTC-week window.
A correctly de-duplicated daily sum equals the weekly value, showing the daily table over-counts via upstream duplication/fan-out rather than the weekly instrument under-counting.

output.claim: The executed events_daily view is defined as `SELECT date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel` — it reads only channel_events_raw with no join, UNION, or self-join.
output.observation: kind=view; ddl="CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel". Only table referenced is channel_events_raw; no join/UNION/self-join; aggregation is COUNT(*).

output.claim: The marts signups view is `SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily` — a pure rename pass-through of events_daily that introduces no additional join or aggregation.
output.observation: kind=view; ddl="CREATE VIEW signups AS SELECT bucket_date AS day, channel, events AS signups FROM events_daily". No join/UNION/aggregation added; signups = events_daily with columns renamed.

output.claim: In channel_events_raw, COUNT(*) = COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) = 4437, so there are zero duplicate event_id rows for the weekly rollup to collapse or the daily path to retain.

source.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS raw_total, COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS raw_distinct FROM channel_events_raw

output.observation: raw_total=4437, raw_distinct=4437 (equal). DDL confirms event_id is TEXT PRIMARY KEY, which by definition forbids duplicate event_id rows.

output.claim: SUM(events) over all of events_daily = 4437 and over all of events_weekly_rollup = 4437, both exactly equal to channel_events_raw's 4437 rows, so neither transformation multiplies rows.

source.query: SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw) AS raw_total, (SELECT SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)) FROM events_daily) AS daily_grand_total, (SELECT SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)) FROM events_weekly_rollup) AS weekly_grand_total

output.observation: raw_total=4437, daily_grand_total=4437, weekly_grand_total=4437 — all three identical. A fan-out or duplication in the daily path would make daily_grand_total exceed raw_total; it does not.

output.claim: For the week of 2026-06-22 the daily-vs-weekly gap (1194 vs 895) is fully accounted for by boundary reassignment of distinct events: 1194 events fall in the KST-date window, 895 in the UTC-week bucket, 800 in both, 394 KST-only, 95 UTC-only, and 1194−895 = 299 = 394−95.

source.query: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT event_id) AS distinct_total, SUM(CASE WHEN date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS in_kst_week, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at)=strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS in_utc_week, ... in_both, kst_not_utc, utc_not_kst FROM channel_events_raw

output.observation: distinct_total=4437, in_kst_week=1194, in_utc_week=895, in_both=800, kst_not_utc=394, utc_not_kst=95. daily_sum_week (1194) equals in_kst_week (1194) — no multiplication on the daily path; the excess is 299 distinct events reassigned across the bucket boundary, not duplicated rows.

output.claim: DataHub UPSTREAM lineage for staging.events_daily returns two upstreams — raw.channel_events_raw and raw.web_sessions — even though the executed events_daily view text references only channel_events_raw.
output.observation: upstreams total=2: raw.channel_events_raw (degree 1, health PASS) and raw.web_sessions (degree 1, health PASS, described as 'one row per visit, is_automated flag not every producer sets'). This is the only artifact inviting an h2 fan-out story, but it is contradicted by e11 (view omits web_sessions) and e14 (daily total equals raw total, so no join fan-out reaches the output).

output.claim: The warehouse view events_daily (mapped to dbt staging.events_daily) is a single-table COUNT(*) over channel_events_raw grouped by date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') — a KST +9h calendar-date bucket — with no join to web_sessions or any other table.
output.observation: warehouse.schema returned events_daily as kind=view with columns bucket_date, channel, events (all TEXT) and ddl: CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel

output.claim: The warehouse view events_weekly_rollup is a single-table COUNT(*) over the same channel_events_raw grouped by strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) — a UTC week bucket with no timezone offset — differing from events_daily only in the time-bucketing expression.
output.observation: warehouse.schema returned events_weekly_rollup as kind=view with columns bucket_week, channel, events (all TEXT) and ddl: CREATE VIEW events_weekly_rollup AS SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel. (This view is not catalogued in DataHub; anchored to its source table channel_events_raw.)

output.claim: Over channel_events_raw for the week of 2026-06-22 the events_daily KST-week sum is 1194 while the events_weekly_rollup UTC-week bucket is 895 (a 299-row / ~33% excess exactly equal to daily_in_weekly_out 394 minus weekly_in_daily_out 95), and re-bucketing the same rows with the weekly rollup given events_daily's +9h offset yields exactly 1194 — closing the gap to zero.

source.query: SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' THEN 1 END) AS daily_sum_kstweek, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-24') THEN 1 END) AS weekly_utc_bucket, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at, '+9 hours') = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-24','+9 hours') THEN 1 END) AS weekly_kst_aligned, SUM(CASE WHEN date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' AND strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) <> strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-24') THEN 1 END) AS daily_in_weekly_out, SUM(CASE WHEN (date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') NOT BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28') AND strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-24') THEN 1 END) AS weekly_in_daily_out FROM channel_events_raw

output.observation: warehouse.query returned one row: daily_sum_kstweek=1194, weekly_utc_bucket=895, weekly_kst_aligned=1194, daily_in_weekly_out=394, weekly_in_daily_out=95

output.claim: Adversarial boundary test of h1: of the events in the events_daily KST-week window for 2026-06-22, all 394 rows that shift out of the events_weekly_rollup UTC-week bucket fall on the single first KST day 2026-06-22 (394 of that day's 413 rows), while interior days 2026-06-23 through 2026-06-28 contribute zero shifted rows.

source.query: SELECT date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') AS kst_date, COUNT(*) AS in_daily_window, SUM(CASE WHEN strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) <> strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-24') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS shifted_out_of_utc_week FROM channel_events_raw WHERE date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28' GROUP BY kst_date ORDER BY kst_date

output.claim: events_weekly_rollup is a live SQL view (kind='view') defined as SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel, so its value is recomputed on every read and cannot be a stored/materialized snapshot frozen from an incomplete or partial load.
output.observation: warehouse.schema returned name=events_weekly_rollup, kind=view, columns=[bucket_week TEXT, channel TEXT, events TEXT], ddl: CREATE VIEW events_weekly_rollup AS SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_week, channel.

output.claim: For week 2026-W25 the events_weekly_rollup reported total (895) exactly equals an independent fresh COUNT(*) over channel_events_raw for the same UTC-week window (895), while the summed events_daily rows for 2026-06-22..2026-06-28 total 1194 (also equal to a fresh KST-date recompute of 1194).

source.query: SELECT strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22') AS target_bucket, (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)),0) FROM events_weekly_rollup WHERE bucket_week = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22')) AS weekly_reported, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw WHERE strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) = strftime('%Y-W%W','2026-06-22')) AS weekly_recomputed_from_raw, (SELECT COALESCE(SUM(CAST(events AS INTEGER)),0) FROM events_daily WHERE bucket_date BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28') AS daily_sum, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw WHERE date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') BETWEEN '2026-06-22' AND '2026-06-28') AS daily_recomputed_from_raw

output.observation: Single row: target_bucket=2026-W25, weekly_reported=895, weekly_recomputed_from_raw=895, daily_sum=1194, daily_recomputed_from_raw=1194. The stored weekly value matches a fresh COUNT over the same UTC window exactly.

output.claim: Bucketing the identical channel_events_raw rows by UTC week versus by KST (+9h) week diverges in every week of the window (W22 593/532, W23 707/702, W24 1123/795, W25 895/1194, W26 972/974, W27 147/240) — including W24 where the UTC-weekly count is higher than the KST-daily sum — yet both methods yield the same grand total of 4437 rows.

source.query: SELECT w.bucket_week, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw r WHERE strftime('%Y-W%W', r.occurred_at) = w.bucket_week) AS weekly_utc_rollup, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM channel_events_raw r WHERE strftime('%Y-W%W', datetime(r.occurred_at,'+9 hours')) = w.bucket_week) AS kst_daily_sum FROM (SELECT DISTINCT strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) AS bucket_week FROM channel_events_raw) w ORDER BY w.bucket_week

output.observation: Rows: 2026-W22 utc=593 kst=532; 2026-W23 707/702; 2026-W24 1123/795; 2026-W25 895/1194; 2026-W26 972/974; 2026-W27 147/240. The UTC column sums to 4437 and the KST column sums to 4437 (identical totals). No week reconciles; direction of the gap even reverses (W24 weekly>daily, W25 daily>weekly).

output.claim: events_daily is also a live SQL view (kind='view') over the same channel_events_raw table (CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel), so the daily and weekly series are two recompute-on-read views of one source, not a rebuilt-daily table versus a frozen weekly snapshot.
output.observation: warehouse.schema returned name=events_daily, kind=view, ddl: CREATE VIEW events_daily AS SELECT date(occurred_at, '+9 hours') AS bucket_date, channel, COUNT(*) AS events FROM channel_events_raw GROUP BY bucket_date, channel. Both events_daily and events_weekly_rollup read the same channel_events_raw; the only difference is the bucketing expression (+9h KST date vs no-offset UTC week).

output.narrative: The daily and weekly series are two recompute-on-read views over the SAME channel_events_raw table that bucket time incompatibly: events_daily buckets by KST calendar date via date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') (e1, e25) while events_weekly_rollup buckets by UTC week via strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) with no offset (e2). For the week of 2026-06-22 the daily sum is 1194 vs the weekly rollup's 895 — a 299-row (~33%) excess — and re-running the weekly bucket with the daily table's +9h offset yields exactly 1194, closing the gap to zero (e3). The gap is pure boundary reassignment of distinct events, not extra signups: 1194 in the KST window, 895 in the UTC bucket, 800 in both, 394 KST-only, 95 UTC-only, and 1194-895 = 299 = 394-95 (e15); all 394 shifted rows fall on the single first KST day 2026-06-22 while every interior day shifts zero (e4) — the signature of a <=1-day timezone offset moving events across the week edge, amplified by the mid-window campaign traffic landing near that edge. The number moved because measurement definitions disagree, not because people acted differently.

alternatives_rejected.hypothesis: h2 upstream_data_defect: the daily path multiplies rows via a web_sessions fan-out join or un-deduplicated ingestion, over-counting signups.
h3 instrument_failure: the weekly rollup is a frozen/materialized snapshot under-reporting because a build failed or loaded a partial partition during the campaign spike.
customer_behavior: the daily-over-weekly excess reflects a real difference in signups (e.g. the marketing campaign) rather than a measurement artifact.

steps.action: Redefine the events_weekly_rollup view via CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, changing the bucket expression from strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) to strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at, '+9 hours') so it uses the same KST +9h offset already applied by events_daily. No other clause changes; it still reads channel_events_raw and COUNT(*) grouped by (bucket_week, channel).
steps.target: events_weekly_rollup (warehouse view; uncatalogued in DataHub, anchored to source urn:li:dataset:(urn:li:dataPlatform:postgres,witnessgraph.raw.channel_events_raw,PROD))
steps.rationale: Root cause is a pure time-zone bucketing mismatch over one shared source: events_daily buckets by KST date(occurred_at,'+9 hours') (e1,e25) while events_weekly_rollup buckets by UTC strftime('%Y-W%W',occurred_at) with no offset (e2). For the week of 2026-06-22 that yields daily=1194 vs weekly=895; re-bucketing the weekly series with the +9h offset yields exactly 1194, closing the gap to zero (e3). The 299-row excess is boundary reassignment of distinct events (800 in both buckets, 394 KST-only, 95 UTC-only; 1194-895=299=394-95) with all 394 shifted rows on the single first KST day 2026-06-22 (e4,e15) — not real over-counting. Aligning the weekly view to the daily view's offset reconciles the two series at the source of the discrepancy.

steps.action: Do NOT modify events_daily or marts.signups; keep the KST daily grain as the canonical reporting timezone and align the weekly series to it (not the reverse).
steps.rationale: The served signups metric marts.signups is a pure rename pass-through of the KST events_daily grain (e12), and DOWNSTREAM lineage shows it feeds marts.signup_conversion_daily, described as 'sensitive to anything that moves the denominator'. Aligning the weekly side to KST (step 1) fixes the symptom while moving zero served values; the alternative of re-bucketing events_daily to UTC would cascade through marts.signups into signup_conversion_daily and change published numbers — a strictly larger blast radius. Direction chosen from lineage, not preference.

steps.action: Add a standing reconciliation assertion: for every KST week, SUM(events) over events_weekly_rollup must equal SUM(events) over events_daily rolled to the same KST week, and each view's grand total must equal COUNT(*) over channel_events_raw.
steps.target: New data test/assertion (e.g. dbt test) over events_weekly_rollup vs events_daily
steps.rationale: Pre-fix the weeks diverge in both directions and never reconcile (W22 593/532, W24 1123/795, W25 895/1194, W27 147/240) even though both view totals equal 4437 (e23,e14). Post-fix they must match week-by-week with the total preserved. A persisted assertion detects any future re-introduction of an offset/bucketing divergence and closes the observability gap that let this ship silently.

steps.action: Register events_weekly_rollup in the DataHub catalog, and add owners plus backfill column schema for marts.signups.
steps.target: DataHub metadata for events_weekly_rollup and marts.signups
steps.rationale: Diagnosis-time accountability gaps: events_weekly_rollup is absent from the catalog (so its downstream consumers cannot be read from lineage and this fix's blast radius cannot be fully enumerated), and marts.signups has no owners and zero recorded schema fields. Cataloguing and ownership make the next incident's lineage, blast radius, and escalation path knowable. Metadata-only; alters no data. Secondary to steps 1–3.

blast_radius: events_weekly_rollup — the redefined view. It is recompute-on-read (e21,e25), so the change takes effect on next read with no stored-data migration. Per-week weekly-signup values shift where events straddle the KST/UTC week edge (e.g. 2026-W25 895→1194, W24 1123→795, W22 593→532, W27 147→240 per e23); the grand total is unchanged at 4437 (e14).

Downstream consumers of events_weekly_rollup (weekly-signup dashboards/reports) — NOT enumerable from lineage: events_weekly_rollup is not catalogued in DataHub (blind spot), so its consumers cannot be read from the catalog and must be identified out-of-band. Any consumer of the weekly series will see the reconciled KST numbers after this change.

marts.signups and its DOWNSTREAM marts.signup_conversion_daily (read from DataHub lineage) — OUT of blast radius: the daily path is intentionally left unchanged (step 2), so no served signups or conversion-ratio values move.
output.verification: Before applying, snapshot the current per-week events_weekly_rollup totals. After CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW, re-run the e22/e3 reconciliation for the week of 2026-06-22: SUM(events) over events_weekly_rollup for the KST week bucket must now equal the summed events_daily rows for 2026-06-22..2026-06-28 (both 1194; the prior UTC value was 895). Then run the e23 sweep across W22–W27: every week's weekly-rollup total must equal the KST daily sum for that week, and both views' grand totals must still equal channel_events_raw's 4437 (e14), confirming the fix only reassigns boundary events and neither adds nor drops any. A zero daily-vs-weekly gap across all weeks with the total preserved = fixed. To revert, restore the prior view definition (strftime('%Y-W%W', occurred_at) with no offset).
